subject: Re: Marketplace security packet — audit logging + KMS language final technical review
body:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 9:12 AM
Subject: Marketplace security packet — audit logging + KMS language final technical review

Marcus — can you do a last technical pass on two sections before we circulate for sign-off + partner submission?

1) Audit logging claim (FAQ + packet)
Current draft text:
- “All administrative actions are recorded in immutable audit logs retained for 1 year.”
- “Customers can request audit log exports upon request.”

2) KMS / encryption keys (FAQ + packet)
Current draft text:
- “All data is encrypted at rest using customer-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS / Google Cloud KMS).”

My concern is we might be over-claiming, but I also don’t want to undersell vs what AWS/GCP reviewers expect.

Attachments:
- marketplace-security-faq-aws-gcp_v7.docx
- marketplace-security-packet-draft_v12.pdf

If you can reply with exact replacement wording (ideally 2–4 bullets each) that we can drop in verbatim, I’ll update today.

Thanks,
Soojin
Product Marketing Lead
Redwood Inference


From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 11:03 AM
Subject: Re: Marketplace security packet — audit logging + KMS language final technical review

Agree we’re over-claiming in both places.

Audit logging:
- “All administrative actions” is too broad unless we define “administrative” and the surface area (Console UI? API? internal ops? underlying cloud provider actions?).
- “Immutable” is a red flag. We have access controls + audit trails, but we do not have a cryptographic immutability guarantee we can defend in a review.
- “Retained for 1 year” is not true as a default across all plans.

KMS:
- “Customer-managed KMS keys” is not accurate for Hosted API in its default setup. We use KMS (AWS KMS / Cloud KMS) but keys are Redwood-managed in our accounts.
- Customer-managed keys (customer-owned KMS) is only applicable for certain Private deployments and/or specific enterprise setups.

Proposed replacement wording (safe + accurate):

A) Audit logs
Option 1 (general + true):
- “Redwood generates audit logs for control-plane events (e.g., user authentication, org and project membership changes, API key creation/revocation, and other administrative actions in the Redwood Console).”
- “Audit logs are stored in Redwood’s centralized logging system and protected by role-based access controls and monitoring.”
- “Audit log retention depends on the customer’s plan and configured retention policy.”
- “Customers may export audit logs via supported mechanisms for long-term retention and SIEM ingestion (availability varies by deployment type).”

B) Encryption / KMS
- “Redwood encrypts customer data at rest and in transit.”
- “For hosted deployments, encryption keys are protected using cloud key management services (AWS KMS / Google Cloud KMS) operated by Redwood.”
- “For Private deployments, customers can integrate with customer-managed keys via supported KMS/HSM options, depending on the deployment architecture.”

Two questions I need confirmed before we finalize:
1) What’s the default retention period we’re committing to for Hosted (and what add-on extends it)?
2) Do we actually have a self-serve export path for audit logs today (vs ‘upon request’), and if so is it customer-facing/documented?

If Olga can answer (1) and someone can confirm (2), I can tighten the language.

- Marcus


From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 12:21 PM
Subject: Re: Marketplace security packet — audit logging + KMS language final technical review

On retention:
- Hosted API: default audit log retention is 30 days today (standard). Enterprise customers can purchase extended retention (90 days / 1 year) as an add-on.
- Dedicated: same as Hosted unless explicitly contracted; most Dedicated enterprise deals are 90 days.
- Private: customer controls retention if logs are stored/exported within their environment; if Redwood is operating the control plane, we align to contracted retention.

We should not say “retained for 1 year” as a blanket statement.

On exports:
- My understanding is exports are currently “supported via request” / guided setup, not a universal self-serve button in Console. (We should avoid implying self-serve unless Eng confirms.)

Also +1 on removing “immutable.” Reviewers often ask what mechanism provides immutability.

Olga
GRC Lead


From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 2:09 PM
Subject: Re: Marketplace security packet — audit logging + KMS language final technical review

Great — with Olga’s retention notes, I’d recommend we use tighter text that doesn’t imply features we don’t have universally.

Suggested final copy (drop-in):

AUDIT LOGGING (FAQ + Packet)
- “Redwood generates audit logs for control-plane activity, including user authentication events and administrative actions in the Redwood Console (e.g., user and role changes, API key creation/revocation).”
- “Audit logs are stored and protected using access controls and monitoring to help detect unauthorized access.”
- “Audit log retention depends on the customer’s plan and configured retention policy (default retention may vary by offering).”
- “For customers with enterprise requirements, Redwood can support audit log exports and/or integrations for long-term retention and SIEM ingestion (availability varies by deployment type).”

Notes:
- I removed “immutable.” If we want to mention integrity, we can say “tamper-evident controls” only if we can point to something concrete. Otherwise keep it generic.
- I avoided “all administrative actions” and instead bounded to “control-plane activity” + examples.

ENCRYPTION / KMS (FAQ + Packet)
- “Redwood encrypts customer data in transit using TLS and at rest using industry-standard encryption.”
- “For hosted deployments, encryption keys are protected using cloud key management services (AWS KMS / Google Cloud KMS) operated by Redwood.”
- “For Private deployments, customers may integrate customer-managed keys via supported KMS/HSM options, depending on the deployment architecture.”

Please also check for any place we say “customer-managed KMS keys” without qualification — that should be removed/changed.

If we want a single-sentence shared responsibility line (helps in marketplace reviews):
- “Security responsibilities are shared between Redwood, the customer, and the underlying cloud provider, depending on the deployment model.”

- Marcus


From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 15, 2025 at 9:07 AM
Subject: Re: Marketplace security packet — audit logging + KMS language final technical review

This direction looks right.

Two notes before we lock:
1) Please ensure “audit logs” does not imply we log customer prompt/response content by default. Buyers ask that immediately.
2) For “industry-standard encryption” we should avoid naming algorithms unless we’re consistent throughout (and unless Security Eng confirms the exact implementation across services).

Soojin — once you’ve incorporated Marcus’ language, route the updated FAQ + packet to me + Olga for final review. I can turn around same day.

Aisha


From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 16, 2025 at 1:26 PM
Subject: Re: Marketplace security packet — audit logging + KMS language final technical review

Updated both docs with your proposed copy + Aisha’s note re: not implying prompt/response content.

New audit logging block (what I’m planning to ship):
- “Redwood generates audit logs for control-plane activity, including user authentication events and administrative actions in the Redwood Console (e.g., user and role changes, API key creation/revocation).”
- “Audit logs are stored and protected using access controls and monitoring to help detect unauthorized access.”
- “Audit log retention depends on the customer’s plan and configured retention policy.”
- “Redwood does not log customer prompt/response content as part of audit logging.”
- “For customers with enterprise requirements, Redwood can support audit log exports and/or integrations for long-term retention and SIEM ingestion (availability varies by deployment type).”

New encryption/KMS block:
- “Redwood encrypts customer data in transit using TLS and at rest using encryption.”
- “For hosted deployments, encryption keys are protected using cloud key management services (AWS KMS / Google Cloud KMS) operated by Redwood.”
- “For Private deployments, customers may integrate customer-managed keys via supported KMS/HSM options, depending on the deployment architecture.”

Marcus — can you confirm this wording is technically accurate as written? If yes, I’ll mark it approved in the packet and send to AWS reviewer tomorrow.

Soojin


From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 16, 2025 at 4:38 PM
Subject: Re: Marketplace security packet — audit logging + KMS language final technical review

Yes — the updated wording is materially accurate.

Two minor edits (optional but I recommend):
1) “Redwood does not log customer prompt/response content as part of audit logging.”
   -> Suggest: “Redwood’s audit logs record control-plane events and do not include customer prompt/response content.”
   (Keeps it scoped to audit logs; avoids broader “does not log” interpretations.)

2) “encrypts … at rest using encryption.”
   -> Suggest: “encrypts … at rest using industry-standard encryption.”
   (It reads better; we’re not naming algorithms.)

Everything else is good from my side.

- Marcus
